questions.question: If the eight -digit number 342x 18y6 is divided by 72, then what is the value of sqrt {9x + y} , for the largest value of y?
questions.solution:
For a number to be divisible by 72, it has to be divisible by 8 and 9.

For a number to be divisible by 8, the last three digits of the number should be divisible by 8.

For maximum value of y 

y = 9 

Now, the number will be 

342x 1896 

For a number to be divisible by 9 the sum of all the digits should be divisible by 9

⇒ 3 + 4 + 2 + x + 1 + 8 + 9 + 6 = 33 + x should be divisible by 9.

⇒ For x = 3, the sum of the digits will be 36 and will be divisible by 9.

∴ √(9x + y) = √((9 × 3) + 9) = √36 = 6

questions.question: Two circles of radii 15 cm and 12 cm intersect each other, and the length of their common chord is 18 cm. What is the distance (in cm) between their centers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7439adc130bf4a53c9217149eb02a0f6faaa1f437d444bd778add72002b08cb3.png] 

Let O and O’ be the center of the circle and PQ be the length of the common chord.

OP = 15, O’P = 12

PM = ½ PQ (as perpendicular from the center of the circle to a chord bisects the chord)

PM = ½ 18

PM = 9

By applying Pythagoras theorem in PMO:

OM² = OP² – PM²

= 15² - 9²

= 225 – 81

= 144

OM = √144 = 12

By applying Pythagoras theorem in PMO’:

O’M² = O’P² – PM²

= 12² - 9²

= 144 – 81

= 63

O’M = √63

O’M = 3√7

OO’ = OM + O’M

= 12 + 3√7

∴ The distance between their centers = 12 + 3√7

questions.question: Two concentric circles are of radii 15 cm and 9 cm. What is the length of the chord of the largest circle which is tangent to the smaller circle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30faca5920987769fcf1e87512381b4ab3403d93be051ca4a96c7e3a58715886.png] 

Let O be the center of the circle, AB be the chord of the largest circle and C be the point on the smaller circle through which the chord passes.

AO = 15 cm and OC = 9 cm

Applying Pythagoras theorem in AOC:

AC² = AO² – OC²

AC² = 15² - 9²

AC² = 225 – 81

AC² = 144

AC = 12 cm

Now, AB = 2AC ( A perpendicular drawn from the center of the circle to the chord bisects the chord)

∴ AB = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

questions.question: If 30 persons take 10 days to complete a certain work working 8 hours a day, then 40 persons should work how many hours a day so that the work is completed in 6 days?
questions.solution:
Men₁ Days₁ Hours₁ = Men₂ Days₂ Hours₂

30 × 10 × 8 = 40 × 6 × Hours₂

Hours₂ = 10

40 people should work 10 hours a day to complete the work in 6 days.

questions.question: If a + b + c = 5, a² + b² + c² = 27 and a³ + b³ + c³ = 125, then the value of 4abc is:
questions.solution:
We have,

(a + b + c)² = 5²

a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca) = 25

27 + 2(ab + bc + ca) = 25

2(ab + bc + ca) = -2

(ab + bc + ca) = -1

Now,

a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = (a + b + c)( a² + b² + c² – ab – bc – ca)

a³ + b³ + c³ – 3abc = (a + b + c)[a² + b² + c² –(ab + bc + ca)]

125 – 3abc = 5 × [27 – ( -1 )]

125 – 3abc = 5 × 28

125 – 140 = 3abc

3abc = -15

abc = -5

∴ 4abc = - 5 × 4 = -20

questions.question: A person sold an article at a loss of 8%. Had he sold it at a gain of 10.5%, he would have received Rs. 37 more. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
**Formula used:**

Loss = C.P - S.P

S.P = [(100 - Loss%)/100] × C.P

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of an article be x

If he sells the article at 8% loss, SP of article = [(100 – 8)/100] x

= 0.92x

If he sells the article at 10.5% profit, SP of article = [(100 + 10.5)/100] x =

= 1.105x

Difference in SP = 1.105x – 0.92x = 0.185x = Rs. 37

⇒ x = 37/0.185 = 200

**∴ C.P of the article is Rs. 200.**

questions.question: In ΔABC, AB = 7 cm, BC = 24 cm and AC = 25 cm. If G is the centroid of the triangle, then what is the length (in cm) of BG?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB = 7 cm, BC = 24 cm and AC = 25 cm

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb80f2298af7eff01cd279b60f70b1c4f7034e69ca71302d5ab88c637266875f.png] 

In ΔABC, AC² = AB² + BC²

ΔABC is right angled triangle at B

Let the coordinates of B = (0 , 0)

Coordinates of A = (0 , 7) and Coordinates of C = (24 , 0)

Centroid (G) of ΔABC = ( {frac{{0 + 0 + 24}}{3} , frac{{7 + 0 + 0}}{3}} )

⇒ Centroid (G) of ΔABC = (8, 7/3)

By distance formula:

BG² = (8 - 0)² + (7/3 - 0)² 

⇒ BG² = 64 + 49/9

⇒ BG2 = 625/9

⇒ BG = 25/3 {{ }} = 8(1)/(3)

**∴ BG is 8(1)/(3)**

questions.question: If cos² θ – sin² θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0, 0° < θ < 90°, then what is the value of 4 cosecθ + cotθ?
questions.solution:
Given: cos² θ – sin² θ – 3cosθ + 2 = 0

⇒ cos² θ – (1 – cos² θ) – 3cos θ + 2 = 0

⇒ cos² θ – 1 + cos² θ – 3cos θ + 2 = 0

⇒ 2cos² θ – 3cos θ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cos² θ – 2cosθ – cos θ + 1 = 0

⇒ 2cosθ (cos θ – 1) – 1(cos θ – 1) = 0

⇒ (2 cos θ – 1)(cos θ – 1) = 0

⇒ cos θ = ½ or cos θ = 1

Cos θ = 1 is not possible as θ < 90°

⇒ cos θ = ½

⇒ θ = 60°

Now, 4 cosec θ + cot θ = 4 cosec60° + cot60°

⇒ 4 cosec θ + cot θ = 4 × 2/√ 3 + 1/√ 3 = 9/√ 3 = 3√

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum for 3 ½ years at 10% per annum is Rs. 2,940. What will be the compound interest on the same sum for 2 ½ years at the same rate when interest is compounded yearly (nearest to rupee)?
questions.solution:
S.I. = PRT/100

⇒ 2940 = (P × 10 × 7/2)/100

⇒ P = Rs. 8400

Now, C.I. on Rs.8400 for first year at 10% rate of interest = 10/100 × 8400 = Rs. 840

⇒ Principal for second year = 8400 + 840 = Rs. 9240

C.I. at 10% for second year = 10/100 × 9240 = Rs. 924

⇒ Principal for last 6 months = 8400 + 840 + 924 = Rs. 10164

As we have to calculate interest for six months, rate of interest = 10/2 = 5%

C.I. at 5% for last 6 months = 5/100 × 10164 = 508.2

⇒ Total compound interest for 2.5 years = 840 + 924 + 508.2 = Rs. 2272.2 ≈ Rs. 2272

questions.question: The ratio of the combined target production of AC Machines In January and April to that of the combined actual production of AC Machine in March and April was:
questions.solution:
Combined target production of AC Machines In January and April = 60000 + 90000 = 150000

Combined actual production of AC Machine in March and April = 100000 + 80000 = 180000

∴ The ratio of the combined target production of AC Machines In January and April to that of the combined actual production of AC Machine in March and April is = 150000 : 180000 = 5 : 6

questions.question: The actual production of AC Machines in April was what percentage more than the average target production of AC Machines over five months?
questions.solution:
The average target production of AC Machines over five months = (60 + 30 + 80 + 90 + 100)/5

= 72

The actual production of AC machines in April exceeds the average target production of AC Machines over five months by 80 – 72 = 8

⇒ 8/72 × 100 = 100/9

= 11(1)/(9)\%

∴ The actual production of AC machines in April exceeds the average target production of AC Machines over five months by 11(1)/(9)\%

questions.question: The total target production of AC Machines in February, April and May was what percentage less than the total actual production of AC Machines over all the five months (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.solution:

The total actual production of AC Machines over all the five months = 70 + 50 + 100 + 80 + 120 = 420

Hence,

(420 - 220)/420 × 100 = 47.6%

∴ The total target production of AC Machines in February, April and May was what 47.6% less than the total actual production of AC Machines over all the five months

questions.question: Two trains of same length are running on parallel tracks in the same direction at 54 km/h and 42 km/h respectively. The faster train passes the other train in 60 seconds. What is the length (in metres) of each train?
questions.solution:
Relative speed of fastest train = 54 – 42 = 12 km/hr = 12 × 5/18 = 10/3 m/s.

Let the length of the train be x metre.

As both the trains are running on parallel tracks in same direction, the distance covered by the fastest train will be x + x = 2x

We have,

Distance/Time = Speed

2x/60 = 10/3

x = 100 metre

∴ The length of each train = 100 metre.

questions.question: The ratio of the incomes of A and B is 2 : 3 and that of their expenditure is 1 : 2. If 90% of B’s expenditure is equal to the income of A, then what is the ratio of the savings of A and B?
questions.solution:
Let the income of A be 2x and income of B be 3x and their expenditure be y and 2y respectively.

90% of B’s expenditure is equal to the income of A.

⇒ 90/100 × 2y = 2x

⇒ 9y = 10x

⇒ y = 10x/9

Savings of A = Income – Expenditure

= 2x – y

= 2x – 10x/9

= 8x/9

Savings of B = Income – Expenditure

= 3x – 2y

= 3x – 2 × 10x/9

= 7x/9

∴ The ratio of the savings of A and B = 8x/9 : 7x/9 = 8 : 7

questions.question: There are 90 students in a class, out of which 70% are from village A and others are from village B. The average score of students from village B in a test is 20% more than that from village A. If the average score of all the students is 53, then what is the average score of the students from village B?
questions.solution:
Students from village A = 70/100 × 90 = 63

Students from village B = 90-63 = 27

Let the average score of students from village A = x

⇒ Average score of students from village B = 1.2 x

⇒ Average score of all the students = [63 x + 27(1.2 x)]/90 = 53

⇒ x = 50 and 1.2 x = 1.2 × 50 = 60

∴ The average score of the students from village B = 60
